title: ALMA detection of CO rotational line emission in red supergiant stars of the massive young star cluster RSGC1. Determination of a new mass-loss rate prescription for red supergiants
question: What are the gas mass-loss rates and wind velocities of red supergiants in the open cluster RSGC1 from ALMA CO(2-1) observations, and what new mass-loss rate prescription can be derived for red supergiants?

recipe.goal: Image continuum, SiO(5-4), and CO(2-1) cubes, extract spectra, and measure source angular sizes
recipe.method: Image continuum (excluding SiO channels), SiO v=3 J=5-4, and CO(2-1) cubes at 3 km/s resolution; locate sources using SiO and continuum peaks; extract CO(2-1) spectra in a 0.75 arcsec circular aperture; create zeroth-moment maps over uncontaminated channels and measure azimuthally averaged radial profiles in 200-mas annuli to determine FWHM and 3-sigma diameters.
key_parameters: Annuli thickness = 200 mas; 3-sigma cutoff = 3 x 25 mJy/beam km/s
assumptions: CO line profiles are intrinsically symmetric around v_LSR, so the uncontaminated red wing can be used to assess ISM contamination on the blue side

recipe.goal: Retrieve terminal wind velocities and CO gas mass-loss rates via non-LTE radiative transfer modelling
recipe.method: Model the CO(2-1) line profiles using the 1D non-LTE radiative transfer code GASTRoNOoM (multi-level approximate Newton-Raphson operator) and ray-trace with a 0.75 arcsec circular model beam to derive v_inf and Mdot_CO for the 5 detected RSGs, upper limits for undetected RSGs, and Mdot_CO for 3 Galactic RSGs.
key_parameters: 150 shells logarithmically spaced from R_star to R_out (R_out = 350 R_star for F01, F13; 400 R_star for F02; 600 R_star for F03, F04)
Turbulent velocity v_turb = 3 km/s; wind velocity exponent beta = 0.5 (R_star to R_dust) and beta = 3 (beyond R_dust)
assumptions: Distance d = 6600 pc; gas kinetic temperature power law with epsilon = 0.6; silicate dust condensing at ~1750 K (R_dust = 3-4 R_star); gas-to-dust ratio r_gd = 200; all photospheric carbon locked in CO giving [CO/H] = 8.9e-5

recipe.goal: Fit Mdot-luminosity-initial mass empirical relations across four open clusters
recipe.method: Re-fit individual cluster Mdot_SED-L_bol relations using IDL FITEXY, then perform multivariate linear least-squares fits with MPFIT and 10^4 Monte Carlo realisations to jointly fit Mdot_SED (across RSGC1, NGC 2100, NGC 7419, chi Per) and Mdot_CO (for F01-F04 in RSGC1) as a function of L_bol and M_ini.
key_parameters: 10^4 Monte Carlo realisations; 68% confidence interval from 0.16 and 0.84 percentiles
assumptions: Common luminosity slope b and initial-mass slope S across all clusters; F13 is excluded as an outlier experiencing a different mass-loss mechanism

recipe.goal: Evaluate stellar evolution implications and lifetime fraction in high mass-loss phase
recipe.method: Compute stellar evolutionary tracks of a 25 Msun star until core carbon depletion using MESA comparing the new RSG mass-loss prescription (Eq. 8) with Nieuwenhuijzen & de Jager (1990), and perform a Bayesian binomial analysis of the fraction of RSG lifetime spent in the strong mass-loss stage.
key_parameters: Initial mass = 25 Msun; convective overshooting = 0.335 pressure scale heights; switch to RSG wind recipe below T = 10^4 K
Beta distribution shape parameters alpha = 2, beta = 14
assumptions: Solar metallicity and metal fractions from Asplund et al. (2009); flat prior on fraction of time F in strong mass-loss stage

score_reason: Public archival ALMA data (2013.1.01200.S), complete tables of input parameters and external cluster data (Tables 1, A.1, E.1, G.1), well-specified regression equations, and public Zenodo files for the MESA models; however, the core radiative transfer code GASTRoNOoM is proprietary and CASA imaging settings are not fully specified.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data and complete tabular data in the paper allow independent reproduction of the continuum flux densities, CO(2-1) spectra, line widths/v_LSR, source sizes, the cluster regression fits (Eqs. 4-8), and the MESA evolutionary tracks (with public Zenodo inlists), while Mdot_CO can be approximated using public radiative transfer codes (e.g. LIME) or the analytical De Beck et al. (2010) formula.
